A.reason: Sound LUCB-style concentration of refinement on cutoff-straddling ideas using the existing BT module, but the acceptance gate is judged by the same in-loop judge family it risks overfitting, and +30-50% cost buys only marginal top-3 changes.

B.reason: Presupposes an executable-check ledger that does not yet exist, doubles development tokens over 1-2 weeks, and its template-reuse premise is doubtful for idiosyncratic idea claims, so the compounding benefit is speculative.

C.reason: Executable falsification is a genuinely independent signal, but for qualitative idea briefs most claims will be not_checkable, leaving s ~ 0 and a selector deliberately blinded to all other information; the sandbox is heavy infrastructure for that risk.

D.reason: Making the system's output a selection from a strict superset of the baseline's candidates gives a non-inferiority floor under one shared assumption (judge-rater correlation), with a logged displacement rate that reveals whether real gain occurs; cheap at one extra single-agent run.

E.reason: Principled Crowd-BT-style reliability weighting at zero extra tokens with a clean offline Kendall-tau test, but it needs ~300 externally rated votes that may not exist yet and noisy a_j estimates could add more variance than they remove.

F.reason: Learning the residual selection error is the right target and the shrinkage-to-current-ranking design is careful, but ~10 labels per brief across heterogeneous briefs plus the Goodhart risk of panel-derived labels make the payoff unlikely within 15 briefs.

G.reason: Depends on an unbuilt contest loop, needs 50 briefs in two arms to detect a 10-point change in an in-loop child-beats-parent rate that is itself only a proxy, and cross-brief operator transfer is an untested hypothesis.

H.reason: Feeds finalists the one signal a lone agent lacks (an independent adversary's loss reasons), constrains length and accepts only both-order wins from a third family so the loop is monotone in a verifier, and the no-reasons control arm cleanly isolates the conditioning effect.

I.reason: Two days of work closes the proxy gap between internal finals and the rated conditions, testable offline by re-judging past finalists; gain is capped by existing finalist quality and carries some LLM-rater overfitting risk.

J.reason: Cheap, offline-testable fix for a plausible presentation deficit unique to multi-agent output (critique residue, cross-references), though the numeric-quantity rule invites invented numbers and yields nothing if idea quality is the real gap.

K.reason: Trivial to build and replay offline, but by its own admission diversification loses under a mean-of-3 metric, which is what pairwise card comparisons against the baseline top 3 effectively measure, and the tau cluster-shift is an unvalidated constant.
